Title: “With them, we felt strong”: captain Teweia Butibara thanks the nation
Excerpt: After lifting the IDC trophy, the Te Eitei captain thanked the I-Kiribati community in Suva, the coaching staff and his teammates.
Body:
Te Eitei captain Teweia Butibara, 27, spoke to Oceania Football Center after leading Kiribati to the 2026 FMF IDC Premier Division title.

He singled out the I-Kiribati supporters living in Suva, who followed the team from the opening defeat to the final, and thanked coaches Pine Iosefa and Tetabo Manaima for their planning and preparation. He delivered his message to the nation in Te Taetae ni Kiribati, and hopes I-Kiribati at home and overseas take pride in what the squad achieved.

Butibara scored Kiribati’s first ever goal at the IDC in the opening match against Seaqaqa, and finished the tournament lifting the trophy.
Image Alt: Kiribati players celebrate together on the pitch
Author: Rafael Saltori

Title: Itiata, Martin Jr and Kiteon sweep the IDC individual awards
Excerpt: Kiribati took all three major Premier Division awards: Golden Ball, Golden Boot and Golden Glove.
Body:
Kiribati didn’t just win the Premier Division. They took all three of its major individual awards.

- **Golden Ball (best player): Nabetari Itiata**, who scored four goals, including two in the final.
- **Golden Boot (top scorer): Bauro Martin Jr**, the 19-year-old from Butaritari, with six goals in four matches.
- **Golden Glove (best goalkeeper): Toom Kiteon**, who kept a clean sheet against Nadroga.

Te Eitei scored 17 goals across their four matches, winning three in a row after losing their opener.
Image Alt: The Kiribati starting eleven in Suva
Author: Rafael Saltori

Title: Te Eitei crowned FMF IDC Premier Division champions
Excerpt: On their tournament debut, Kiribati beat Seaqaqa 6–1 in the final at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva to win the Premier Division title.
Body:
Kiribati’s men’s national team are champions of the Premier Division at the 86th FMF Inter-District Championship. Te Eitei beat Seaqaqa FC 6–1 in the final at HFC Bank Stadium, Suva, on Sunday 11 October.

It was Kiribati’s first appearance at the IDC, and the first time in the competition’s history that Fiji Football has invited another nation to take part.

## How the final unfolded

The teams went in level at 1–1 at half-time. Seaqaqa were reduced to ten men just before the hour, and Te Eitei took control. Nabetari Itiata, who scored twice, restored the lead early in the second half, and the second half finished with five unanswered goals, including strikes from Peter Diehm and Bauro Martin Jr.

The scoreline carried extra meaning. Seaqaqa had beaten Kiribati 4–2 in the opening match, so the final was a chance to put that right, and the players took it.

## A squad built on sand

Many of this squad learned the game on sandy pitches, as there is no grass pitch in Kiribati. After the opening defeat, Te Eitei beat Nadroga 6–0 for the first win in the senior team’s history, then knocked out Fiji’s Under-17 side 3–1 in the semi-final.

The coaching staff thanked the I-Kiribati community in Fiji, and especially the students from the University of the South Pacific who came out in numbers to support the team at every match.

The title came with a $6,000 prize. Kiribati also swept the individual awards: Nabetari Itiata took the Golden Ball, Bauro Martin Jr the Golden Boot and Toom Kiteon the Golden Glove.

Title: From 47 years without a win to champions
Excerpt: Oceania Football Center on how Kiribati went from a winless senior history to IDC champions in a single week.
Body:
Oceania Football Center’s report on the 6–1 final win over Seaqaqa at HFC Bank Stadium, which completed a remarkable turnaround: before this tournament, Kiribati’s senior side had never won a match.

The full report covers the final, the red card that changed it, and what the title means for football in Kiribati.
Image Alt: Kiribati players celebrate a goal in Suva
Author: Rafael Saltori

Title: From Butaritari to IDC history: meet Bauro Martin Jr
Excerpt: A profile of the 19-year-old Tekinati FC forward who finished the tournament as Golden Boot winner.
Body:
Bauro Martin Jr grew up on Butaritari and plays his club football for Tekinati FC. At 19, he became the first player known to score four goals for Kiribati’s senior team, and went on to win the IDC Golden Boot with six goals in four matches.

Oceania Football Center spoke to him about his journey from the outer islands to the IDC.
Image Alt: Kiribati in action at the IDC
Author: Rafael Saltori

Title: Te Eitei beat Fiji Under-17 to reach the IDC final
Excerpt: Goals from Peter Diehm, Bauro Martin Jr and Nabetari Itiata sent Kiribati into the Premier Division final against Seaqaqa.
Body:
Kiribati are through to the Premier Division final of the 86th FMF Inter-District Championship after a 3–1 win over Fiji’s Under-17 national team at Buckhurst Park, Suva.

Peter Diehm, Bauro Martin Jr and Nabetari Itiata scored for Te Eitei against a Fiji side preparing for the Under-17 World Cup. Oceania Football Center has a [full report on the semi-final](https://oceaniafootballcenter.org/2026/10/10/kiribati-stun-world-cup-bound-fiji-u17-to-reach-historic-idc-final/).

Kiribati will face Seaqaqa FC in the final at HFC Bank Stadium. Seaqaqa came from a goal down to beat Tavua 3–1 in the other semi-final.
Image Alt: Kiribati players celebrate a goal together

Title: A win 47 years in the making: Kiribati 6, Nadroga 0
Excerpt: Bauro Martin Jr’s hat-trick earned the senior team the first win in its history and a place in the semi-finals.
Body:
Kiribati beat Nadroga 6–0 at HFC Bank Stadium to record the first win in the senior team’s history and qualify for the semi-finals. Before this tournament, Te Eitei’s recorded history was 11 matches at the South Pacific and Pacific Games, with no wins.

Bauro Martin Jr scored a hat-trick, with Nabetari Itiata, Booia Maitina and Kiniore Teofilo Siu also on the scoresheet. Because Nadroga are a district side, the result doesn’t count as an official international win, but it was the first time a Kiribati senior team had walked off the pitch as winners.
Image Alt: Kiribati in action at the IDC
Author: Rafael Saltori

Title: From sand pitches to IDC history: Teweia Butibara on Kiribati’s challenge
Excerpt: The Te Eitei captain explains what it takes for players raised on sand to compete on grass in Fiji.
Body: Most players in Kiribati grow up playing on sandy surfaces. Captain Teweia Butibara told Oceania Football Center why competing on proper grass pitches in Fiji was both the biggest challenge and the biggest opportunity of the IDC.
Image Alt: The Kiribati team line up in Suva
Author: Rafael Saltori

Title: Kiribati’s IDC debut carries a bigger ambition
Excerpt: Before a ball was kicked, Oceania Football Center looked at what the IDC means for Kiribati’s place in Oceania football.
Body: Ahead of the tournament, Oceania Football Center previewed Kiribati’s first IDC and the ambition behind it: proving that Te Eitei belong on Oceania football’s next stage.

Title: KIFF Pro League: first round complete, League 1 and League 2 confirmed
Excerpt: The top eight teams form League 1 and will play for the title and a place in the OFC Professional League 2027.
Body:
Mauri! The first round of the KIFF Pro League is complete, and the rankings have now decided who plays in League 1 and League 2.

The top eight teams form League 1. The remaining teams make up League 2.

## What happens next

Each league now plays a further round. League 1 will decide the KIFF champion, who will represent Kiribati in the **OFC Professional League 2027**.

League 2 teams play their own round, competing for a place in League 1 under the new promotion and relegation system.

For any questions, please contact the KIFF office. Kam rabwa!

Title: Kiribati invited to the FMF Inter-District Championship
Excerpt: For the first time in the tournament’s history, Fiji Football has invited another nation to compete at the IDC.
Body:
Te Eitei will compete at the 86th FMF Inter-District Championship in Fiji, the first time a nation from outside Fiji has been invited to take part in the competition.

Fiji Football chief executive Mohammed Yusuf described the invitation as a historic occasion for the tournament.

Kiribati will play in the Premier Division alongside Fiji’s Under-17 side and the district teams. This year’s IDC runs across three divisions of eight teams each.
